_source: Numeric rule constants transcribed from Core v1.21 (entry numbers in 'src'); the engine code implements the procedures. tests/unit/rules_consistency.test.js asserts that every constant still appears in the verbatim Core text (content/rules_text.json).

strength._rule: 4.3.0-c.6.6.5 (live 15.10.2026): a creature's Defeat XP also weighs how much stronger its own numbers are than an ordinary creature of the same Level and type (this reference, scaled like any creature): durability (HP raised by its average DEF/MDEF at defense_weight per point) times ATK, over the reference's, square-rooted and capped at max. Ordinary fauna (rat, wolf, boar, deer, horse, serpent ...) stay at their Level's XP; heavy body plans and strong individuals give more; never less than before.

settlements._rule: 4.3.0-c.6.6.5 (live 15.10.2026: the Ashbridge Market District at midday felt like an empty stage, and finding a buyer for monster parts took a failed SEARCH and an hour). A settlement's size (its content sub: capital, seat, city; a settlement the story created is a village until the content says otherwise) decides how busy its streets are by time of day and which everyday trades it has. The crowd is ambient: scene colour, never stored as people; someone becomes a person when they matter (spoken to, acting, trading, in danger, attacked). The trades are functions, not a fixed list of named shops: an ordinary trade of the settlement is found without a check by day (signs, open fronts, asking around); the story names and places the shop when Alaric goes there, and a shop already established stays the one he knows.

city.day: crowded: residents and stallholders, customers haggling, carts and porters, a draught animal or a herd driven through, craftsmen at open fronts, now and then folk of other peoples
city.evening: thinning: the last customers and stallholders packing up, lamplighters, people heading home or to the taverns
city.night: near empty: a watch patrol, a late drinker, shuttered fronts

town.day: busy: townsfolk at their errands, a few stalls and carts, craftsmen at work
town.evening: quiet: people heading home, a tavern's noise

village.day: a few villagers at their work, children and animals
village.evening: quiet doorsteps and a lit window or two

trades.name: hunter's exchange / monster-parts buyer (buys hides, pelts, fangs, claws, scales, venom, chitin)
general store (rope, lamps, rations, travel gear)
apothecary / alchemist (remedies, potions, herbs; buys venom and herbs)

difficulty_scores._note: PROPOSED helper scale (not in Core): named Difficulty Scores for Difficulty Checks; Core #7 only requires a fixed Difficulty Score.

creature_detection._note: PROPOSED: direct-stat creatures have no PER; their Detection Score for Core #8 Stealth vs Detection defaults to the Human baseline PER 5 unless Content gives the species a detection value.

guild.src: Lorebook v0.12 GUILD — Contract lifecycle (live run 27.09.2026 04:11)
guild.contract: A Guild contract (a quest with a Guild Quest Rank) is taken at the Guild and completed only when the player turns it in (his message says so: by name, or unnamed when it is the one active contract) in a city or capital with a Guild branch; the Guild accepts a turn-in once the story has credibly achieved the contract's desired outcome; posted proof is expected verification/world guidance, not an exclusive token checklist. The engine then pays the posted reward, one fixed payout, and Quest XP. Local clients inform, give access and confirm proof; they neither complete nor pay it. Work without a Quest Rank is private and settles directly (Quest XP, no Guild credit). The Guild registration is a procedure, not a contract.
guild.registration_fee_src: Canon decision 27.09.2026: 2 silver = 20 cp at every branch (docs/RUNTIME_V4_PLAN.md §6.4)

drive_off._doc: Prototype C (4.3.0-c.6.6.6): a contract whose desired outcome or title allows the targets to be driven off (one of the verbs with off/away/out after it, or one of the words alone) counts each one the engine saw flee a fight with Alaric (escaped) as driven off; one the story only lets walk out of the scene is not (src/v4/guild.js defeatTally).

supported_ranks._status: proposed (plan D10): runtime defaults for branches without their own list

time.src: Runtime V4 time caps per reply (docs/RUNTIME_V4_PLAN.md §6.7); runtime defaults, no world law

engine_clock.src: Prototype C only (setting 'planner'; docs/PROTOTYPE_C.md §11): engine-owned time. Provisional values, no balance

recovery.src: Prototype C only (docs/PROTOTYPE_C.md §11): natural recovery while resting or sleeping, the same basis for both: per hour of booked rest or sleep, in % of the maximum, rounded down, never above the maximum. Provisional values, no balance

exploration.src: Patch 6 (docs/PROTOTYPE_C.md): obstacles and hazards of a place (src/v4/features.js). Provisional values, no balance
exploration.harm_note: what a hazard (or an obstacle that can hurt) costs Alaric when an engine check against it fails or a hidden one catches him, by the feature's difficulty; HP never below 1 by a hazard of a place, STA never below 0
exploration.tool_note: a tool he holds and uses for an attempt makes it this many difficulty steps easier

travel.src: Patch 5 (docs/PROTOTYPE_C.md): travel legs on the planner path. Provisional values, no world law
travel.leg_event_note: the share of travel legs beyond a settlement that may bring one concrete interruption (an encounter, an obstacle, a meeting) the story makes fit the land; the others are uneventful. Never a guaranteed fight, never what it is

combat.wary_note: Patch 4: a creature or person that fought Alaric, or watched his fight from the scene, stays aware of him this long; a story that says it lost track of him sooner sets no Ambush (only his own stealth check does)

items.src: Patch 3 (4.3.0-c.6.6.11): how a thing behaves when Alaric uses it (src/v4/items.js); runtime defaults, no world law
items.note: A thing is a tool (used, not used up) unless its name says it is food or used up when used. Food counts in portions (one portion is one meal) and keeps for a while, preserved food longer. Gear with a slot is equipment. Whole words of the thing's name decide.

living.src: Patch 8 (Living Dungeons, src/v4/living.js, docs/PATCH8_LIVING_DUNGEONS.md): what a true Dungeon gets when it is first established, where its own content entry (lore.json dungeons[].living) says nothing. Fixed into the campaign's events at its establishment; a later change here never changes an established Dungeon. Provisional values, no balance
living.role_spans_note: the level window of each encounter role on a level of a Dungeon, as parts of that level's Rank band (F: 1-14 gives minion 1-5, guard 4-8, boss 5-9); never outside the band, never Alaric's level
affiliations: hired blades of a local house

return_stone.name: Return Stone
return_stone.text: a palm-sized grey stone etched with a gate rune; crushed in the hand inside a Dungeon, it carries its holder back to that Dungeon's gate

living.pace_note: the quiet parts (no engine encounter) a level may have before each of its encounters, drawn per cycle from this list: a level is never an endless string of empty rooms, and never a fixed number of rooms
